prompts.display_text: Pin a country with a temple standing today that Ulisses Soares dedicated or rededicated.
prompts.text_original: A country where Ulisses Soares dedicated or rededicated a temple now in use (as of October 2026).
prompts.citation: ChurchofJesusChristTemples.org chronological list (dedicated-by column), read 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: Ulisses Soares dedicated Fortaleza Brazil and Arequipa Peru in 2019 and Feather River California in 2023. In 2025 he dedicated Bahía Blanca Argentina and Nairobi Kenya, the first temple in Kenya.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory whose first temple was dedicated while Russell M. Nelson was Church president.
prompts.text_original: A country whose first temple was dedicated while Russell M. Nelson was Church president.
prompts.citation: Church temple list (first dedication per country) and presidency dates
prompts.summary: Russell M. Nelson was President of the Church from 2018 to 2025, and many countries and territories received their first temple in that time. President Nelson dedicated Rome Italy in 2019, and first temples followed in Haiti, Portugal and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (2019), Guam and Cape Verde (2022), Puerto Rico and Thailand (2023), and Kenya and Côte d'Ivoire (2025).

prompts.display_text: Pin a country or territory where Haitian, Papiamento, Bislama or Tok Pisin is official.
prompts.text_original: A country or territory where a creole language with a Book of Mormon edition (Haitian, Papiamento, Bislama, Tok Pisin) is official
prompts.summary: Book of Mormon text exists in creole languages including Haitian Creole (full text 1999), Tok Pisin of Papua New Guinea (2002), Bislama of Vanuatu (2004) and Papiamento (selections 1987). Papiamento is spoken in Aruba, Curacao and Bonaire.

answers.name: Haiti
answers.fact: Haitian Creole selections came in 1983 and the full text in 1999.

answers.name: Papua New Guinea
answers.fact: The Tok Pisin Book of Mormon appeared in 2002.

answers.name: Aruba
answers.fact: Papiamento, given selections in 1987, is official in Aruba.

answers.name: Curacao
answers.fact: Papiamento selections appeared in 1987.

answers.name: Vanuatu
answers.fact: Bislama selections came in 1985 and the full text in 2004.

answers.name: Caribbean Netherlands
answers.fact: Papiamento, given selections in 1987, kept its official status in the Caribbean Netherlands, which includes Bonaire, in 2010.

prompts.display_text: Pin a present-day country holding a place named in Isaiah's oracles against the nations (Isaiah 13-23).
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place named in Isaiah's oracles against the nations (Isaiah 13-23)
prompts.note: Places in the West Bank or Gaza, such as Bethlehem, Hebron, Jericho or Gaza city, count as Palestine, which is not an answer.
prompts.summary: In Isaiah 13 to 23, the prophet delivers burdens, or warnings, against the nations around Judah. They open with Babylon's fall and include Egypt, Damascus, Moab, Tyre and Sidon, and the Arabian oasis of Tema. Isaiah also names Elam and Media, and Cush, the Nile land south of Egypt (Isaiah 20:3-5).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Babylon's fall opens the oracles (Isaiah 13).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Isaiah 19 is the burden of Egypt.

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Assyria took Ashdod, a Philistine city now in Israel (Isaiah 20:1).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Moab gets two chapters (Isaiah 15-16).

answers.name: Lebanon
answers.fact: Isaiah 23 laments Tyre and Sidon.

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Damascus will become a ruinous heap (Isaiah 17:1).

answers.name: Iran
answers.fact: Elam and Media are called to attack Babylon (Isaiah 21:2).

answers.name: Saudi Arabia
answers.fact: Tema, the oasis of Tayma, is told to bring water (Isaiah 21:14).

answers.name: Sudan
answers.fact: Isaiah 20:3-5 names Ethiopia (Cush), the Nile land from Syene to near Khartoum.

prompts.display_text: Pin a formerly communist country that Saints names as newly open to missionaries about 1991.
prompts.text_original: Saints vol. 4 ch. 26: around 1991, missionaries were newly permitted in these formerly communist countries. Pin one.
prompts.summary: As communist governments fell around 1989 to 1991, countries that had kept missionaries out began to let them in. Saints vol. 4 ch. 26 names Poland, Hungary, Bulgaria, Romania, Slovenia and Croatia among the newly opened countries.
